quotes_used_verbatim: Cruise ships under our jurisdiction are subject to two inspections each year.
These inspections are periodic and unannounced.
We post all inspection scores and reports. Find details, including descriptions of violations and how the ship addressed them.
We use a 100-point scale to score cruise ships
Cruise ships fail inspections when they score 85 or below.
primary_sources.verification_note: The 85-or-below failure threshold first appeared in a search summary. It was NOT printed on that basis - the FAQ page was fetched directly to obtain the sentence verbatim before any number was published.

claims.derived_arithmetic: That 86 is the pass mark is stated as following directly from CDC's published 'fail at 85 or below'. No independent claim.
claims.not_claimed: NO specific fleet average, NO distribution statistics, NO claim about how many ships fail, NO named ship's score, and NO claim about what any particular ship scored. Statements that scores cluster high are framed qualitatively as an interpretive caution, not as a measured statistic. The vessel-jurisdiction criteria (passenger count, voyage type) are NOT stated because the fetched page did not specify them.
claims.interpretive_framing: The weighting of violation categories (food/water/handwashing above documentation) and the trend-over-single-score advice are the site's own editorial reasoning about how to read published reports, not CDC guidance.
claims.internal_anchor: The high-score-but-dirty-cabin point is anchored to our own published Getaway Aug 2026 logbook, and exists partly to give the two existing CDC/norovirus news pieces an evergreen page to link to.

voice_audit.scope: full article body (itemprop=articleBody), not the summary
voice_audit.machine_tell_scan: 0 banned cruise-marketing terms, 0 generic AI tells, 0 copulative-avoidance constructions (serves as / stands as / represents a / embodies / marks a / constitutes), 0 translationese terms, 0 inline self-correction leakage, 0 ellipses.
voice_audit.corpus_comparison: em-dash density and sentence-length variance compared against four published InTheWake articles (cruise-tipping-2026, what-cruise-actually-costs-2026, great-stirrup-cay-changes-2026, cruise-pool-lifts-accessibility-gap), whose measured em-dash densities span 7.7-16.0 per 1000 words. This page falls inside that range.
voice_audit.corrections_applied: cruise-passport-or-birth-certificate: 'careful rather than comprehensive' changed to 'careful rather than complete' (one generic-AI-tell hit). No other page required an edit.
voice_audit.honest_limit: This attestation records a mechanical scan plus author judgment. It measures the presence of known tells and structural variance; it cannot certify that the prose reads as lived experience to a human reader.
